observationsNotFindings: The subject spells the word four times as 'remasurement' or 'remasures' while spelling it correctly twice elsewhere in the same file, in remeasurementClause and in 'may remeasure OBL-JOIN-FX-EXECUTION'. I did not charge it. It is an orthographic slip, not a coined term — the correct spelling in the same document settles that — and it asserts nothing false and leaves nothing undecidable. Worth a note only so the coordinator is not left wondering whether 'remasurement' names something distinct from remeasurement. It does not.

The real risk this cycle was staleness, not argument. Between the previous dispatch and this one, HEAD advanced two commits, D-167 added a live DR-G31 row, required-now moved 26 to 27, and both file 08 and COORD changed digest. A document assembled from the previous cycle's values would still parse, still read fluently, and fail only at the digests. Every one of the nineteen recordedInputs entries carries the new value.

Because G31 actually became live, the delicate conditional arithmetic in the predecessor family collapses to a simple one. The earlier act had to say 26, then 27 if G31 lands, then 28, and had to supply a fallback for G31 never landing. Here the register shows 27 of 27 and the subject states a single 27-to-28 step. The fallback is no longer needed and is correctly absent rather than carried forward as dead text.

Two claims in this subject are checkable statements about live cells rather than assertions about itself — the owner derivation from DR-114 and DR-G12, and the DR-G09 owner and claim cells in liveG09ClaimDoesNotOwnThisProperty. All four cell values match the live register exactly. A document that quotes the register to justify staying off another gate's territory is easier to audit than one that simply promises not to trespass.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: No blockers, no should-fix. 21 attacks run, 21 refuted. The governing state moved since the last cycle in this family, so I re-measured everything: HEAD is c983aa2 (D-168), D-167 put a live DR-G31 row on file 08, the condition-4 cell now reads 27 of 27 with 31 of 31 owners, and both file 08 and COORD changed digest. Staleness was the likeliest failure and it does not occur — all 17 basedOn pins and all 19 recordedInputs carry the new values, including file08Pin 9af2bc71 and COORD 8a061a67, and every one recomputes. JFXG-V1-B1 is landed in all three forms the dispatch names: artifactExists is true against v1's false, the named path exists on disk with a digest equal to the pinned specification, and occupancy is asserted in the present tense with no deferral construction anywhere. I verified the blocker's substance without reading Codex — frozen v1 says artifactExists false while the file it names exists at 59030 bytes — so the landing was judged against the filesystem rather than either reviewer's account. The owner 'Operability + security' equals both the live DR-114 and live DR-G12 cells by ==, and the subject's quoted DR-G09 owner and claim cells also match the live row exactly, which is how it justifies staying off G09 rather than merely promising to. The thirteen classes are ordered-equal to both live actor-join v8 and frozen v1, with exactly thirteen FC-JOIN tokens in the file. G32 has zero live rows and required-now stays 27. One correction on my own record: the blocker landed here is Codex's, and I missed the same false premise when I reviewed the dependent three-limb act last cycle — I read a predecessor's 'artifactExists was false at naming time' as history rather than testing it. That is recorded under reviewerSelfCorrection. A spelling slip, 'remasurement' for 'remeasurement', appears four times and is not charged; the file spells it correctly twice elsewhere.
